## Routines ship with the package: nightly package updates as the first standard

Adopting projects ran their nightly package updates as hand-written scheduled tasks, each a little different. Weeks
of runs showed what goes wrong:

- **Persistent sessions get expensive.** A routine bound to one session re-reads its whole history on every fire:
  150k to 240k tokens per run after a month, several times the cost of the same work in a fresh session.
- **Conditional "no release" rules expire.** "No release until the owner says the server is ready" stopped being
  true; a persistent session remembered the go and released and deployed every nightly bump, migrations included.
- **A skills bump without a state refresh turns CI red.** A new skills version can change `context/state.json`; the
  bump has to regenerate it and run the doctor in the same pull request.

New in this release:

- `routines/` ships in the package. `routines/package-updates.md` is the standard nightly routine: every
  `@softure-ai/*` package and SOFTURE pin to the newest, `@softure-ai/skills` included (installer, `state`,
  doctor at 0), one pull request through the chain, merged on green, a report on every run. Hard rules it states:
  never release, tag, publish or deploy, without conditions; one pull request at most; never force a package;
  never disable or edit the routine; rely on the repository, not on memory.
- `routines/README.md`: the standard every routine follows (a fresh session on every fire, state in the repository,
  one routine per purpose per project, the schedule in the project's `timezone`) and the prompt that sets the
  routine up. The scheduled task holds only a pointer prompt, so the routine follows the installed package version
  and is never re-created to pick up a fix.
- `context/workflow.json` → `routines.packageUpdates.hold`: packages held back by an open issue, kept in the
  repository so a fresh session finds them (WORKFLOW §2).
- WORKFLOW §13 Routines; README section; the release gate checks every routine carries the hard rules and is listed.

Adopting projects: delete the old package-update scheduled task, then paste the setup prompt from
`routines/README.md` into the project's main chat.
